name: be_1r
lesson: Break-even at +1R gives back more than it saves: many winners dip back to the entry after +1R and still reach 1.5R.

name: tp_125
lesson: A 1.25R target wins only slightly more often and gives up 0.25R on every winner; 1.5R stays better.

name: tp_2
lesson: Most moves do not reach 2R before the stop: 1.5R stays the better target.

name: session_04_20
lesson: The late hours are weak only in the second half of the history; cutting them hurts the first half. Hour filters look regime-dependent, so the running session challengers must prove themselves forward.

name: lookback_15
lesson: A 15-candle stop is wider, so many more setups pass the 1.5% minimum, and those extra setups lose. The 10-candle swing and the 1.5% minimum work as a pair.

name: session_08_24
lesson: The night hours (00-08 UTC) are weak only in the 2nd half of the history: cutting them helped overall but made the 1st half worse (+0.165R vs +0.198R). Like session_04_20, hour filters are regime-dependent on this history; only forward data (session_07_21, session_13_21) can settle them.

name: exit_opposite_signal
lesson: Closing on the opposite Q-Trend trigger of the same chart cuts more winners than it saves losers: worse in both halves (+0.065R and +0.179R) and PF 1.41. A flip on the trading chart is mostly noise inside the trade; the fixed 1.5R target and swing stop stay better, as with be_1r.

name: stop_floor_1_5pct
lesson: Widening tight swing stops to 1.5% instead of skipping them adds about 920 trades that lose (-0.016R overall, -0.076R in half 1, max DD 66.1R vs 11.1R). The 1.5% minimum does not work by keeping costs low per R: it removes bad entries. A tight swing means a choppy, low-range setup, and a wider stop does not fix it. Keep skipping them.

name: limit_rest_5min
lesson: A limit order resting 5 minutes fills 10 more trades, and they lose: +0.229R vs +0.254R, worse in both halves. If the price only comes back to the limit after the first minute, the move has already stalled (adverse selection). Fill in the first minute or skip, as now; market_entry's extra fills are not worth chasing either.

name: stop_mult_075
lesson: A stop at 0.75 of the swing (same target price) is past the sweet spot: +0.293R vs +0.259R but PF 1.53 vs 1.56 and half 1 +0.195R vs +0.198R. Tightening further stops out more winners that first dip about 0.3-0.8R against, and the cost per R rises; the gain from 0.8 to 0.75 is gone. Do not tune the multiplier lower.

name: stop_mult_080
lesson: A stop at 0.8 of the swing is better in both halves (+0.224R vs +0.198R, +0.370R vs +0.320R) with the same PF 1.56, but only +0.038R overall, below the 0.05R bar, with DD 13.2R vs 11.1R. Most of the gain is the bigger win in R on the same exits, not better trades; 0.75 is already worse, so it is a flat, small edge on a 100-day sample. Worth a 4-year check in research tools before any new proposal.

name: min_stop_175
lesson: A 1.75% minimum stop is worse in both halves (-0.012R and +0.286R against +0.178R and +0.336R), PF 1.30. The setups with stops between 1.5% and 1.75% are not the marginal ones; they carry much of the edge. With 1.0%, 1.75% and 2.0% all worse, 1.5% is a clear peak: do not tune min_stop_pct again.

name: lookback_8
lesson: An 8-candle swing stop is worse in both halves (+0.071R and +0.302R against +0.178R and +0.336R), PF 1.41. With lookback 15 also worse, 10 candles is the right swing for this setup: a shorter swing lets different, weaker setups pass the 1.5% minimum instead of only the strong ones. Do not tune stop.lookback around 10.

name: max_candles_48
lesson: Closing at market after 48 chart candles lowers the drawdown (7.0R vs 11.1R) but cuts the slow winners: +0.148R vs +0.258R, worse in both halves (+0.040R vs +0.178R). Trades that run long still reach the target often enough; the 26 history timeouts already earn +0.18R. A time exit is not the fix for the 44 stops that first reached +0.5R.

name: be_125
lesson: Break-even at +1.25R is worse in both halves (+0.142R and +0.313R against +0.178R and +0.336R), PF 1.51, just like be_1r. Winners often touch 1.25R, dip back to the entry and still reach 1.5R. Break-even rules do not work with this 1.5R target at any level tested; do not propose more.

name: macd_trend_filter
lesson: MACD trend filter is worse in both halves on v4 (half 2: +0.335R vs +0.415R, PF 1.49 vs 1.58). Unlike ZL or HTF filters that hurt only half 1, this hurts the strong period too. Like Supertrend direction, most trades already agree with the MACD side; the trades removed are not the bad ones.

name: confirm_window_2
lesson: Removing only 3rd-candle confirmations still hurts: half 1 +0.097R vs +0.109R. Late confirmations (candles 2-3) are good trades; every reduction of the confirmation window removes value. Window=3 is the right setting on this baseline, confirmed now from both ends (window=0 and window=2 both worse).

name: htf_1h_4h
lesson: htf=1h+4h has only 13 trades in half 1 (needs 15). With 4 months of history, any filter requiring both 1h and 4h ZL agreement is too restrictive to screen. Do not propose htf=1h+4h or any stricter HTF combination until the history grows to at least 2 years.

name: stop_mult_120
lesson: A 1.2x wider stop earns less per trade (+0.217R vs +0.264R, PF 1.53 vs 1.58), consistent with the 1h anchor result (wider stops = higher win rate, lower R per trade). The trade's 15m swing at 1.0x is the right width; widening it in either direction on the standard or 1h scale reduces expectancy. Do not test wider multipliers.
